proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline functional must state the accepted all-radius frontier and its radius-adaptive attaining estimator, rather than only the fixed-radius specialization.
proposed_core_edits.proposed: For \(q_C=(C-1)/C\) and \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\), \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C)}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}\{(T-\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C))^{-1}\sum_{t=\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C)+1}^{T}Y_t\prod_{j=t-\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C)}^{t}e(A_j\mid X_j)/b(A_j\mid X_j)\}\), and, uniformly over \(C\ge1\), \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\asymp_{t_0,\zeta}T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Hu--Wager entry must identify the uniform frontier as the sole headline while distinguishing the transferable hard-subclass converse from the upper theorem, which is only for the present bounded-reward binary-action specialization.

proposed.comparator_claim: Hu and Wager's Theorem 3.1 gives the single-trajectory partially observed minimax exponent under their Model 3 conditions, and Section 3.2 asks whether a matching hard construction can also satisfy hidden-state distributional overlap. The present bounded-reward, binary-action hard subclass answers that converse question: because the subclass is contained in any larger Hu--Wager class admitting these instances, its lower bound transfers upward by subclass inclusion. The matching all-\(C\) upper theorem is claimed only for this paper's bounded-reward, binary-action specialization.

Strong or square-integrable stationary density-ratio control supports root-\(T\) behavior for truncated doubly robust evaluation in fully observed MDPs, while heavier ratio tails produce slower regimes.
Latent-state density-ratio coverage is weaker than belief coverage, and future-dependent value guarantees can retain exponentially large outcome or belief quantities without the stronger conditions.
Generic partially observable off-policy evaluation can have arbitrarily large bias, while recovery in the decoupled POMDP uses invertibility and conditional-independence structure.
Double reinforcement learning attains the semiparametric efficiency bound in observed Markov models using estimated \(q\)-functions and marginalized density ratios.
Long-run average policy outcomes admit estimation and confidence intervals in a fully observed Markov mobile-health model.

prose_updates.tldr: For the bounded-reward, binary-action, single-trajectory specialization of Hu and Wager's finite-state Model 3 studied here, the exact cardinality-uniform minimax risk is, uniformly over every \(C\ge1\), \(T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\), where \(q_C=(C-1)/C\) and \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\); the comparison constants depend only on \(t_0,\zeta\). The observable radius-adaptive partial-history estimator attains this surface, with an exact elbow at \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\) and no logarithmic loss. The signed-depth family gives the matching all-estimator converse while preserving bounded latent stationary occupancy. Thus the risk surface is continuous through its \(q_C\)-amplitude and boundary layer even though the pointwise fixed-\(C\) exponent is parametric at \(C=1\) and slower for every fixed \(C>1\). The fixed-radius, equality-boundary, and shrinking-radius results are corollaries of this uniform headline.

project_justification.gap: HuWager2023 establishes the unrestricted partially observed minimax exponent and asks whether its converse can be realized with distributionally overlapping hidden states. Its original hard chain does not provide a cardinality-uniform all-radius risk surface under \(d_e\le Cd_b\), while fully observed stationary-ratio methods cannot use a ratio carried by an unobserved state.
project_justification.niche: The paper's sole headline is the cardinality-uniform observable-data minimax surface over all \(C\ge1\) in the bounded-reward, binary-action, single-trajectory specialization of Hu and Wager's finite-state Model 3. It resolves both the shrinking-overlap boundary layer and the fixed-radius regimes without proxy, emission-rank, finite-memory, or known-latent-dynamics assumptions.
project_justification.fill: Radius-sensitive PHIW bias and covariance bounds yield the uniform upper surface, attained by a radius-adaptive observable history depth. A signed-depth reset family, together with the verified uniform terminal-posterior and observed-path KL bounds, yields the matching two-point converse with constants depending only on \(t_0,\zeta\). The fixed-\(C\), \(C=1\), and shrinking-radius statements follow as specializations. An interval-certified \(360\)-state insulin-policy adaptation demonstrates why bounded latent occupancy need not justify immediate weighting.

sampling_model.design: One behavior-stationary trajectory from a time-homogeneous finite POMDP with binary actions and rewards bounded in absolute value by one; the model is the paper's specialization of Hu and Wager's finite-state Model 3, and the union allows unrestricted finite observed- and latent-state cardinalities.

prose_updates.related_work: HuWager2023 is the theorem and application anchor: its Introduction develops partial-history weighting for partially observed Markov evaluation, its upper analysis balances geometric forgetting against policy-ratio growth, Theorem 3.1 supplies the unrestricted depth-chain converse, and Section 3.2 asks whether an overlapping hidden-state hard family can retain that difficulty. The uniform-overlap frontier answers that converse question inside the present bounded-reward, binary-action specialization and simultaneously gives its matching upper bound. The lower construction is a hard subclass, so its converse transfers by subclass inclusion to a larger Hu--Wager class containing those instances; the upper theorem is not asserted over Hu and Wager's full conditional-moment or general-finite-action class. MehrabiWager2025 studies observable stationary density ratios in fully observed MDPs, where truncation and ratio-tail conditions can yield root-\(T\) behavior; those methods do not reveal the latent ratio here. ZhangJiang2024 distinguishes latent-state density-ratio coverage from the stronger observable operator control needed for future-dependent values. TennenholtzShalitMannor2020 obtains POMDP recovery under decoupling and matrix invertibility, conditions deliberately absent here. KallusUehara2020 and LiaoKlasnjaMurphy2021 provide fully observed efficiency and long-run inference comparators. LuckettEtAl2020 and MaahsEtAl2012 motivate Hu and Wager's glucose application; this paper uses only a finite discretized adaptation and does not claim that the original continuous simulator belongs to the present contraction-and-overlap class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The headline theorem is uniform over \(C\ge1\) for the paper's bounded-reward, binary-action, single-trajectory finite-state specialization, with risk comparison constants and a large-sample threshold depending only on \(t_0,\zeta\), not on \(C\) or either state-space cardinality. The fixed-\(C>1\) exponent, the \(C=1\) parametric endpoint, and the shrinking-radius phase diagram are corollaries of the continuous all-radius surface; only the pointwise fixed-\(C\) exponent jumps at the boundary. The converse uses a hidden alphabet whose cardinality grows as \(O(\log T)\), so it does not settle classes with a uniformly bounded latent alphabet. Honest single-trajectory confidence intervals, policy-learning regret, and empirical testability of latent stationary overlap remain separate questions. The finite insulin adaptation supports interpretation but does not establish membership of the original continuous simulator in the finite-state uniform contraction-and-overlap class.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The terminal-posterior recursion, stationary initial windows, and observed-path chain-rule KL required by the signed-depth converse have been proved, and the finite insulin adaptation's immediate-weight bias has an interval certificate. The remaining scope limitations are substantive rather than proof gaps: the minimax result concerns point-estimation MSE rather than honest inference or policy-learning regret; latent stationary overlap is not made observable or testable; the hard family's latent cardinality grows with \(T\); and the finite insulin adaptation does not certify the original continuous simulator's membership in the paper's finite-state uniform contraction-and-overlap class.

statement_notes.justification: This is the sole headline: it gives one explicit observable estimator and a matching all-estimator converse for the complete all-\(C\) risk surface, with constants independent of \(C\) and of both state-space cardinalities.
statement_notes.gap: HuWager2023 leaves the distributionally overlapping hidden-state converse unresolved and does not provide the continuous shrinking-radius surface under latent stationary overlap.
statement_notes.consumer: A latent physiological occupancy assurance justifies shorter histories only through its quantitative radius: parametric precision occurs in the boundary layer \(q_C=O(T^{-1/2})\), while a fixed nonunit radius retains the partial-observability penalty.

statement_notes.justification: This is the fixed-\(C>1\) specialization of the uniform-overlap frontier, obtained because \(q_C\) is then a positive constant.
statement_notes.gap: It records the pointwise consequence of the uniform theorem rather than serving as a separate headline.
statement_notes.consumer: For a fixed nonunit latent occupancy radius, bounded stationary overlap alone does not certify parametric precision or a universally fixed short history.

statement_notes.justification: This is the \(C=1\), hence \(q_C=0\), specialization of the uniform surface and gives the parametric immediate-weighting endpoint.
statement_notes.gap: The pointwise fixed-\(C\) exponent changes at \(C=1\), but the headline risk surface itself remains continuous through the radius amplitude and its \(T^{-1/2}\) boundary layer.
statement_notes.consumer: Exact equality of target and behavior stationary laws permits immediate weighting; approximate equality must be compared with the sample-size-dependent radius threshold.

statement_notes.justification: This is the shrinking-radius specialization of the uniform theorem, using \(q_{1+\delta_T}=\delta_T/(1+\delta_T)\), which is uniformly comparable to \(\delta_T\) once \(\delta_T\to0\).
statement_notes.gap: It closes the formerly open local transition and identifies the exact elbow \(\delta_T\asymp T^{-1/2}\) without a logarithmic loss.
statement_notes.consumer: It converts a quantitative sequence of increasingly strong latent occupancy assurances into the exact history depth and precision regime.

statement_notes.justification: The finite construction translates the uniform theorem's implication into the published glucose-policy setting without claiming that the continuous simulator satisfies the class.
statement_notes.gap: The refreshed \(360\)-state adaptation now has an interval-certified nonzero immediate-weight bias together with explicit finite contraction, policy-overlap, and stationary-overlap bounds.
statement_notes.consumer: It demonstrates why bounded latent dietary occupancy alone does not license current-action weighting for an insulin threshold policy.
